evidence: Highly structured directory hierarchy with clear separation by OS (Linux, Mac, Windows) and functional domains (config, softwares, lib, DPAPI)
50 packages with low average fan-out (3.22), indicating cohesive internal modules with limited cross-module dependencies
Module-based design where each software (e.g., browsers, chats, sysadmin) is encapsulated in its own subpackage under 'softwares/'
Shared core functionality (crypto, config, write_output, module_info) is centralized in 'config/' and reused across modules
No explicit inter-service communication patterns or network boundaries; all components run as a single application
Each module inherits from a common base class (ModuleInfo), enforcing a consistent interface while allowing OS-specific implementations
Repository depth of 7 levels supports deep but flat module hierarchy typical of monolithic applications with layered organization
risks: Tight coupling between OS-specific modules (e.g., Windows-specific DPAPI logic embedded in core flow) may hinder maintainability
Shared crypto and memory libraries are duplicated across OS directories, risking inconsistency and maintenance overhead
Lack of explicit dependency injection or inversion of control may reduce testability and flexibility
